headline: Class 3
Class 2
plan.evidence: Mazamas grade the route 'B' (basic glacier climb); Mountaineers run it as a Basic Glacier Climb; TR: 'dirt scramble & snow climb', 'wide-open snowslopes to the summit'; glacier is low-angle (7,000 to 6,000 ft over ~1 mi).

Both MP Mega Slab routes: thousands of feet of 4th class/low 5th slab, then '3 pitches of 5.6+' on the summit block; separate TR rates the summit-block chimney '5.6-ish'. One party soloed it, calling it 'pretty easy but exposed'.

AAJ FA account: '10 pitches, 4 of class four and the rest class five with occasional pins for aid. NCCS III, F7, A1'; TR cites the route as 'grade III, 5.7, 10 pitches'. MP/SummitPost: 'a difficult Pete Doorish route that has gone free at 5.10' on the east buttress.

before.rock_grade: Class 3 (brief exposed Class 3-4 moves at the summit block)

body.rock_grade: Class 3 (brief exposed moves at the summit block)

headline: Class 3
Class 3
plan.evidence: 2025 trip report: 'mostly class 2 scrambling with a couple of class 3 moves' to the summit; 2018 party: class 2 scrambling on the north side of the summit block.

headline: Class 4
plan.evidence: 2020 report via the NW gully to the ridge: loose class 3 then 'a short section of exposed class 4 just below the true summit'; hike2hike: final ridge 'several class 4 moves', '3rd and 4th class'; SummitPost: summit block '4th class/low 5th' for ~20 ft.

body.rock_grade: Class 4 (4th class to the col, 3rd class to the summit)

headline: Class 4
plan.evidence: Trip report: steep snow gully to the East-West col, 'some 4th class' to the saddle, then 'easy 3rd class terrain to East McMillan's summit'; a 2025 North Buttress party 'downclimbed SW to the col with West McMillan' before rappelling.

headline: AI3
AI3+
plan.evidence: A 2018 TR grades the Rankin Creek line AI3+: 30-40 deg snow, a 50-ft serac crux of '70-85 degree snow' over a crack bridge, a 60-deg hidden gully, snow arêtes, a 50-deg final gully. Other TRs: 60+ deg, a narrow gully 'the steepest slope of the route', tools and pickets, no grade.

headline: Class 3
Class 2
plan.evidence: 2024 Ptarmigan TR: Lizard 'via the south ridge and descended via the west ridge. The climb is pretty straightforward, but somewhat loose class 2.' SummitPost: an easy ascent from the 6,800-ft pass on the south ridge.

Mazamas 'Gunsight Peak, SW Face': 'A 5.6 rock climb', citing Beckey's Cascade Alpine Guide. CascadeClimbers thread: 'Beckey lists the SW face of the main peak as a sustained 5.6'. Wildsnow: about 5 short pitches, a loose blocky start, then 'wonderful easy climbing up cracks and knobs' on the ridge.

AAJ 1975 (Markov party, first ascent): '1700 feet, NCCS II, F 6', 'a pleasant alpine scramble with two pitches of harder climbing on the steepest part of the ridge'. Beckey's description, quoted in a 2009 attempt report, matches but gives no number.

headline: Class 4
plan.evidence: From the Barrier notch: drdirtbag, 'Degenhardt's 4th class summit'. Chasingdonuts, following Beckey's 'obvious ledge behind the N skyline': 'The route could all be 3rd and 4th class to the summit', with a low 5th move only where they missed a bypass gully. Malclimbs: 30 minutes from the Barrier. Abegg calls the route low 5th, and a party that went off route roped up for about 5.7.

The 1929 Chute-Kaartinen line is the North Face Route of the North Peak, 'Grade III, Class 5.6'; a 2020 report: 'the North Face has ended up with a sandbagged 5.6'; a 2016 report climbs the NE Rib, then 'thick jungle climbing for three rope lengths' to the great bowl and the north rib.

before.rock_grade: Class 3-4 scramble (crux ~100 ft summit step, locally graded 3.5)

body.rock_grade: Class 2 (talus and scree; easy summit scramble)

headline: Class 3
Class 2
plan.evidence: Peak page: from Lyman Lake 'cross-country through open meadows and then talus/scree (Class 2) on south side', 'scrambling is required to reach the summit'; a trip report scrambles a gully and the SW ridge to the top with no harder moves reported.

AAJ 1979 FA account: rappel from the Goode-Storm King saddle onto the glacier, then the '3000-foot rock rib' to the main (east) summit; roped 'leads' with runners on trees, mostly loose rock, steps kicked in snow mid-face, steep snow gully to bypass a steepening; ~12 hours. No difficulty grade given.

headline: WI2
WI2
plan.evidence: Mountain Project route page: East Face, WI2 Steep Snow, 2 pitches, 200 ft; 'obvious cleft on the East Face', steep snow with 'short sections of moderate ice' in cold spells; ice axe(s) and a few screws if belayed.

headline: Class 3
Class 2
plan.evidence: Summer: 'Tailgunner is an easy hike up some slabby rock', an hour's add-on from Gunn; the Gunn/Tailgunner/Wing approach is Class 2 scrambling with bushwhacking. Early season a party cramponed the north slope and a relic-cornice headwall, with no class given.

before.rock_grade: 3rd-4th class with a few moves of low 5th (unrated)

headline: Class 3
plan.evidence: Abegg's Southern Pickets 2 lists 'Pyramid (West Ridge, 3rd)', 'a fun and easy scramble'; SummitPost Picket Range page lists The Pyramid as class 3 for non-technical Picketeers; one trip report recalls 'a few moves of low 5th to leave the ridge' coming from Degenhardt.

headline: Class 4
Class 4
plan.evidence: Trip report on the Middle Finger from the glacier bivy: 'Solid 3rd and 4th class scrambling led to looser 3rd class up higher', no rappels needed; a 2009 traverse report calls the Middle Finger 'a fun snow route'.

before.rock_grade: Class 4-5 (low 5th class scrambling; no specific YDS number grade attested)

plan.evidence: Country Highpoints: 'crux 5.4 pitch', short, exposed; Lemke: '1-2 5.4 moves to get up a flake/crack'; another report: 'the low fifth class section' in the chimney; another: one '5.fun' pitch on a flake with a chimney above.
MP: Open Book 'Easy 5th', 50 ft, wide left-leaning cracks right of the Classic Route; SummitPost Unicorn Peak page lists the 'Open Book Cracks' as Class 5.0.

headline: WI4
WI4
plan.evidence: MP route literally named 'unknown' at Upper Black Ice and Winter Ice Crag (Exit 38): WI4 M4, 70 ft, toprope, right of CYA; formed in the Feb 2019 ice year, 'a fun and interesting dry tool'.

headline: Class 4
Class 4
plan.evidence: NW Shoulder: steep snow traverses averaging ~35 deg, icy, pickets; summit 'class 3-4 rock later in season'; Wikipedia: 'exposed scrambling, class 3'; late season with an open moat '5th class rock for 60 feet or so'.
